script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Pakistan terms Afghan claims regarding Angoor Adda incident 'fabrication of lies'.

- Military Times, 21 hours ago: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract.

After creating a new directorate on warfighter optimization within the Department of Defense, the Pentagon announced it will form a federal advisory committee to weigh in on issues affecting troop performance and health.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan terms Afghan claims regarding Angoor Adda incident 'fabrication of lies'.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Pakistan terms Afghan claims regarding Angoor Adda incident 'fabrication of lies'.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Wednesday dismissed a statement by Afghanistan’s defence ministry regarding the firing at Angoor Adda border area, terming it a “fabrication of lies”. Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the border area in Lower South Waziristan on Tuesday. The attack, which violated border protocols, claimed the life of one local and injured five, while provoking a swift response from security forces.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: ‘Have no illusions’: Kundi tells Afghan Taliban Pakistan will not tolerate attacks after Angoor Adda firing.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned on Wednesday the latest instance of firing from across the Afghan border in Lower South Waziristan, asserting that Pakistan would “never tolerate” attacks on its people or violations of its sovereignty. The incident took place on Tuesday night when Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area. The firing resulted in the death of a local resident and left five of a family injured as a mortar landed on their house.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47bn, according to Pentagon estimate.
The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25 per cent higher than the Defense Department’s estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its estimate, which has not been shared publicly. The disclosure about the rising cost of the Iran war comes as Republicans wrestle with the political fallout of the unpopular conflict ahead of the November 3 election that will determine control of Congress for the next two years.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 9 India-sponsored terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR.
Nine India-sponsored terrorists were killed in two separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Wadh districts, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday. In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that on October 26, security forces conducted IBOs in the districts on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

Tragedy struck when Janardan Changya Gowari, a spokesperson for Shiv Sena, lost his life in a road accident on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His motorcycle was tragically hit by a speeding SUV driven by Mahesh Shivdas Hirve at Adghar village phata. The police have taken swift action, booking Hirve for causing Gowari's death and invoking several legal provisions, as CCTV footage from a nearby hotel captured the shocking incident.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Spain train crash: Drone footage captures twisted carriages as toll tops 60.
The crash occurred along the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line in Toledo province, where two trains carrying hundreds of passengers were travelling in the same direction towards Seville in southwestern Spain, according to Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government. Spain's rail infrastructure operator ADIF said the accident took place on Wednesday morning.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: 63 in 100 Indian pilots may be sleepy during dawn landings, safety review warns.
A new evaluation reveals that approximately 63 out of 100 Indian pilots may be drowsy during dawn landings. This study examined how India's regulations on pilot working hours influence alertness on nighttime flights. It raised concerns about the sufficiency of current guidelines in combating pilot fatigue, with many aviators frequently reporting exhaustion while on duty.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Alastair Campbell on Trump, political violence and why populist politics doesn’t work - podcast.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: Alastair Campbell on Trump, political violence and why populist politics doesn’t work - podcast.
It’s election season: the US midterms are just days away and Israel, Brazil and Serbia have all had consequential elections this week. Alastair Campbell from The Rest is Politics podcast co-host speaks with political editor Tom McIlroy about our ‘high-octane political environment’ and why he argues that populist politics began in the aftermath of the global financial crisis. Following last week’s alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines, Campbell also reflects on how the UK responded to violence towards its own politicians – including Jo Cox, David Amess and Ann Widdecombe.

The head of Australia's national broadcaster says One Nation's depiction of Bluey ramming politicians with a car potentially breaches intellectual property rights. Managing director Hugh Marks describes the rightwing populist party's use of the globally beloved character as 'shocking and disrespectful'. Marks tells Senate estimates he became aware of One Nation's 2024 political cartoon last week and sought legal advice. 'We will be taking further action, I can assure you,' he says.
